title: You stood on the platform.
paragraphs:
You stood on the platform.
You lifted your hands in worship.
You opened the Bible.
People listened when you spoke.
But when nobody was around, you were losing battles you swore you had already won.
And the terrifying part is this:
Most people around you have no idea.

You know how to say the right things.
You know how to pray publicly.
You know how to lead devotionals, encourage broken people, quote Scripture, and carry responsibility.
But late at night, the secret comes back.

The lust.
The bitterness.
The addiction.
The pride.
The hidden conversations.
The compromise.
The rage.
The hypocrisy you keep trying to bury under ministry activity.
And now the question keeps haunting you:
“Can God still use me while I struggle with sin?”
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
There is a difference between a leader who is fighting sin and a leader who is hiding in sin.

One is at war.
The other is making peace with darkness.
That difference changes everything.
Because every believer struggles with sin.
Even the apostle Paul wrote:
“For I do not do the good I want, but the evil I do not want is what I keep on doing.” — Romans 7:19

Paul was not glorifying sin.
He was exposing the war inside every genuine believer.

The Christian life is not sinless perfection.
It is continual repentance and surrender to Jesus Christ.
But some people use “nobody is perfect” as a shield while secretly feeding the very thing Christ died to destroy.
God saw it.
You knew.

And deep down, you know whether you are resisting sin…
or protecting it.

There are leaders publicly preaching holiness while privately nurturing compromise. They cry during worship and return to hidden pornography. They preach forgiveness while secretly living in bitterness. They tell others to trust God while their own hearts are chained to pride, greed, and rebellion.
Outward ministry can continue long after inward intimacy with God starts dying.
That is the danger.
Jesus warned about this kind of spiritual deception with terrifying clarity:
“This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.” — Matthew 15:8
Read that again.
Your gift can still function while your heart drifts.
Your talent can still impress people while your soul starves.
You can build a public image while privately collapsing.
That is why ministry success is not proof of spiritual health.

Judas walked with Jesus.
Judas heard the sermons.
Judas saw miracles with his own eyes.
And still betrayed Christ.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
The real issue is not whether you struggle.
The real issue is what you do with the struggle.

Do you confess it?
Do you fight it?
Do you bring it into the light?
Do you repent when convicted?
Do you hate the sin or secretly love it?
Because Scripture says:
“Whoever conceals his transgressions will not prosper, but he who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy.” — Proverbs 28:13
Mercy is available.
But hidden rebellion hardens the heart.

Some leaders are exhausted not because ministry is heavy…
but because secret sin is draining the life out of them.

Sin always demands secrecy.
Jesus calls you into light.
And eventually, one of them wins.
You cannot continually feed darkness and expect intimacy with God to remain untouched.
You cannot secretly bow to sin and expect peace in your spirit.
You cannot lead people somewhere you refuse to go yourself.

That tension you feel?
That conviction you keep trying to silence?
It is mercy.
Because God disciplines those He loves.
The Holy Spirit convicts before destruction comes.
But many people mistake delayed judgment for God’s approval.
That is dangerous.
Samson kept playing with compromise until the presence of God left him and he “did not know that the Lord had left him.” (Judges 16:20)
Imagine that.

Still moving.
Still speaking.
Still functioning.
But empty.
That should terrify every leader living a double life.
Yet this is where the Gospel becomes more than religious language.
Because Jesus Christ did not come merely to expose sin.
He came to save sinners.

Not polished people.
Not fake perfect leaders.
Not performers.
Sinners.

Broken people.
Ashamed people.
Secretly exhausted people.
People like you.

The cross was never permission to continue in rebellion.
It was the doorway into freedom.

Jesus carried the wrath your sin deserved.
He died in your place.
He rose again so your chains would not have the final word.
That means you do not have to stay divided forever.
Real repentance is possible.
Restoration is possible.
Purity is possible through the power of the Holy Spirit.
But repentance costs pride.

You may have to confess.
You may have to step back temporarily.
You may have to kill the image people have of you.
But better a wounded reputation than a dead soul.

David fell into horrific sin.
Adultery.
Deception.
Murder.
Yet when confronted, he broke before God in repentance.

Psalm 51 was not written by a man protecting his image.
It was written by a shattered man crying for mercy.
“Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.” — Psalm 51:10
That prayer still matters today.
Because hidden sin does not disqualify you from running to Jesus.
Refusing to repent does.
Some of you reading this are exhausted from pretending.
You smile publicly while secretly drowning.
You keep leading while spiritually bleeding.

And every time conviction hits, you promise God:
“Tomorrow I’ll change.”
But tomorrow keeps moving.
Meanwhile your heart grows colder.
Listen carefully:

God is not asking for your performance.
He is demanding your surrender.

Not partial surrender.
Not selective obedience.
Everything.

The sin nobody knows.
The habit you renamed.
The compromise you justified.
The secret messages.
The hidden tabs.
The pride you baptized as confidence.
Bring it into the light.
Now.
Because the most dangerous place to be is spiritually active while spiritually dead inside.
Jesus did not die so you could become better at hiding.
He died to make you free.
And freedom starts where honesty begins.

So yes…
you can lead others while struggling with sin.
Every true believer struggles.

But no…
you cannot safely lead while secretly embracing rebellion and refusing repentance.
Eventually the hidden thing becomes the destroying thing.
And some of you already know exactly what God is confronting right now.
You felt it while reading this.
God saw it.
You knew.
If this exposed something in you, stop defending it and surrender it to Christ completely. Someone else reading needs the courage to repent too.
